Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From d2324a9317f00013facb0ba00b00440e19d2af5e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Christian Brauner <brauner@kernel.org>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 14:50:10 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] nsfs: tighten permission checks for handle opening

Even privileged services should not necessarily be able to see other
privileged service's namespaces so they can't leak information to each
other. Use may_see_all_namespaces() helper that centralizes this policy
until the nstree adapts.

Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260226-work-visibility-fixes-v1-2-d2c2853313bd@kernel.org
Fixes: 5222470b2fbb ("nsfs: support file handles")
Reviewed-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
Cc: stable@kernel.org # v6.18+
Signed-off-by: Christian Brauner <brauner@kernel.org>

diff --git a/fs/nsfs.c b/fs/nsfs.c
index be36c10c38cf..c215878d55e8 100644
--- a/fs/nsfs.c
+++ b/fs/nsfs.c
@@ -627,7 +627,7 @@ static struct dentry *nsfs_fh_to_dentry(struct super_block *sb, struct fid *fh,
 		return ERR_PTR(-EOPNOTSUPP);
 	}
 
-	if (owning_ns && !ns_capable(owning_ns, CAP_SYS_ADMIN)) {
+	if (owning_ns && !may_see_all_namespaces()) {
 		ns->ops->put(ns);
 		return ERR_PTR(-EPERM);
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

The patch modifies a single file (`fs/nsfs.c`) to tighten the permission check when opening namespace file handles. Specifically:

- In the function `nsfs_fh_to_dentry`, the condition for denying access was changed from:
  - `ns_capable(owning_ns, CAP_SYS_ADMIN)` (requires `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` in the owning namespace)
  - **to**: `may_see_all_namespaces()` (a centralized helper that enforces a stricter policy)

**Relationship:** The change replaces a capability-based check with a policy-based helper that prevents even privileged services from indiscriminately viewing other privileged services' namespaces, addressing potential information leakage. This is part of a broader visibility fix for the namespace filesystem (nsfs).

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>
if (owning_ns && !ns_capable(owning_ns, CAP_SYS_ADMIN)) {
</text>
Reason:
This check allowed any process with CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the owning namespace to open file handles to that namespace, even if the process belonged to a different privileged service. This overly permissive permission enabled potential information leakage between namespaces of separate services.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
if (owning_ns && !may_see_all_namespaces()) {
</text>
Reason:
The fix replaces the permissive `ns_capable` check with the `may_see_all_namespaces()` helper, which enforces a centralized policy that restricts cross-service namespace visibility, thereby preventing unauthorized access.
